experiment: reuse one bounded work-stealing pool for module parsing and type checking
hypothesis: Avoiding a second Rayon pool and worker startup should reduce check-subset wall time and peak memory without changing results.
measurement: Quill front-end check-subset profile; not comparable to cargo build or a Rust compile-time result
measurement_method: Linux wait4 rusage for one quillc process; perf_counter wall time; ru_maxrss in KiB.

before.pool_lifecycle: module parsing pool dropped, then a separate type-check pool created

after.pool_lifecycle: the caller retains the parse pool and passes it into type checking

interpretation: No measurable speed or memory improvement; differences are within run noise. Retained to enforce a single pool lifecycle across phases, not as a claimed optimization.
correctness_gate: workspace tests, Clippy with warnings denied, formatting, and 3454-body corpus check passed
